scenarios.title: halo rev A sounder: 15 nF bender, 100 R series, anti-phase from two GPIO at 4.0 kHz, 2.0 V cell at 60 ohm
scenarios.why: the low end of a Ø20 mm bender's free capacitance

constants.name: cp_F
constants.source: the low end of a Ø20 mm bender's free capacitance

constants.name: f_res_est_Hz
constants.source: design.py, lane G: the 7BB-20-3's free resonance is 3.6 kHz. The drive is run at 4.0 kHz, near but not on it.

constants.name: rs_ohm
constants.source: lane G's 500 ohm, carried in design.py, read as a series loss resistance. NOTE THIS READING IS UNCERTAIN: |Z| of 25 nF at 4 kHz is 1592 ohm, so 500 ohm may instead be the motional resistance AT resonance, which is a different element.

constants.name: r_drive_ohm
constants.source: nRF54L GPIO output resistance in HIGH DRIVE. Nordic's standard drive is nearer 100 ohm; the high-drive figure is taken as 40 ohm. NOT FETCHED FROM THE DATASHEET - it is an estimate, and the peak current below is inversely proportional to it, so this is the largest uncertainty in this study.

constants.name: vdd_V
constants.source: end-of-life cell OCV — TI SWRA349's stated threshold. Driving from the WORST rail, not the nominal one.

constants.name: f_drive_Hz
constants.source: near the Ø20 bender's free resonance, design.py: 3.6 kHz. The drive is a square wave because a GPIO has no other shape.

constants.name: r9_ohm
constants.source: R9 on the schematic: series damping on one leg, so a GPIO edge into a capacitive load is not an unlimited current spike off the bulk capacitors

measurements.name: v_bender_pp_V
measurements.why: the swing ACROSS the bender. D11a's whole claim is that two anti-phase pins give the same 2 x VDD a bridge-tied amplifier would.

measurements.name: i_peak_mA
measurements.why: the PEAK current one pin sources — the edge spike, not the sinusoidal average research/05 §11.6 computes

measurements.name: i_rms_mA
measurements.why: the RMS current, which is what the cell and the bulk actually have to supply for the length of an alert

measurements.name: v_rail_min_V
measurements.why: the rail while the sounder runs. A DULT alert lasts seconds; the radio's droop lasted a millisecond.

measurements.name: rail_droop_mV
measurements.why: how far the rail falls while sounding

asserts.name: v_bender_pp_V
asserts.why: D11a's claim is 2 x VDD peak to peak, the same swing a bridge-tied class-D gives. 1.5 x VDD is that with room for the drive and series resistance; below it the anti-phase trick is not working and the amplifier was not free to delete.

asserts.name: i_peak_mA
asserts.why: an nRF54L GPIO in high drive is specified in the single-digit to low-tens of mA. 25 mA is the ceiling this study will call safe without the datasheet figure in hand.

asserts.name: v_rail_min_V
asserts.why: the SoC has to stay alive while it is making a noise. Below 1.7 V it browns out mid-alert, which is the one moment DULT requires it to be audible.

scenarios.why_verdict: 3 assert(s) evaluated, all held; 5 measurement(s) read
scenarios.raw_note: deleted; rerun with --keep-raw, or `ngspice -b -r sounder_15nf_rs500.raw sounder_15nf_rs500.cir`

asserts.name: i_peak_mA
asserts.why: THIS ONE IS MEANT TO BE HIGH. In the low-loss model the edge is limited by the pin's own 40 ohm and the bender's 32 ohm, so the spike approaches VDD/72 = 28 mA.
